newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico regulators chose legislative process.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico regulators chose legislative process.

text.p: The New Mexico Public Utility Commission accepted a proposal by the Public Service Co of New Mexico to seek legislative changes to introduce competition into the state's retail electric power market, the utility said Wednesday.

In an order issued Tuesday, the commission called for a series of meetings including all interested parties to craft legislation for consideration by the New Mexico Legislature in January 1998, the company said.
El Paso Electric Co, Southwestern Public Service Co and TNP Enterprises Inc also operate there.
To facilitate that collaborative process, the commission suspended its earlier order requiring PS New Mexico to file an electric rate case in June, the company said.

However, the commission indicated it will order that rate case filed September 1 if the parties in the negotiations fail to reach consensus on an industry restructuring plan by August 1. By May 13, the participants must file a plan outlining how the process will proceed and establishing a date by when their restructuring proposal will be filed with the commission.

In its order, the commission outlined three broad subjects which must be addressed -- financial and economic issues, consumer protection and environmental issues, and timing of the transition to a competitive market.
